At its September 3, 2026 meeting, the Planning Board, after careful consideration and deliberation, took the following vote relative to the proposed zoning amendments to Section 2007.2 to allow multifamily buildings to consist of more than one building per lot. MOTION: Moved by Moschella, seconded by Brown-Anson, and voted 5:0:0 to initiate the proposed zoning amendment as further amended below to allow multifamily buildings to consist of more than one building per lot in the Central Commercial, General Commercial, Limited Commercial, and General Industrial zoning districts. --~ 200-7.2. Multifamily dwellings. A. Special permit required. The Zoning Board of Appeals may grant a special permit for multifamily dwellings under the following procedures and requirements. Multifamily dwellings in open space/cluster developments shall also comply with the requirements of ~ 200-7.1 of this ordinance. B. Procedure. (1) Applicants shall submit seven (7) copies of an application and the proposed site plan, prepared by a registered engineer, architect, or other qualified professional, showing proposed structures, parking, drives, landscaping, topography and drainage, plus architectural elevations of all proposed buildings and any other site plan submittal requirements specified in the Site Plan, ~ 200-8.4 of this ordinance. Where the development of a Priority Development Site (PDS) requires a special permit hereunder, the aforesaid application and site plan shall be submitted simultaneously The City of Greenfield is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer, a designated Green Community and a recipient of the “Leading by Example” Award with any other permit application(s) required (a) by this Ordinance or (b) by the Code, generally, relating to the use or development of land, buildings or structures and not otherwise exempted by G.L. c. 43D. [Subsection 1 amended by Town Council on October 21, 2009] (2) Within ten (10) days of its receipt, one (1) copy of the application and site plan shall be forwarded by the Clerk of the Board of Appeals to the Planning Board, who shall submit a report of recommendations to the Board of Appeals within thirty (30) days. (3) The Board of Appeals shall not hold a public hearing on the application until receipt of the Planning Board report, or until forty-five (45) days has lapsed from the date of filing. Where the special permit sought hereunder is for the development of one (1) or more multifamily dwellings on a Priority Development Site (PDS), the Zoning Board of Appeals shall render a decision thereon no later than one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of submission of the application. (67) Parking areas shall be screened from public ways and adjacent properties by building location, grading, fencing, or planting. Parking shall be off-street and shall provide for forward moving ingress and egress onto any traveled way. No parking area shall contain more than thirtysix (36) parking spaces. The Planning Board requests the initiation of the attached zoning amendments in order to allow residential adaptive reuse of accessory structures by Special Permit. The zoning amendment includes a new section in the “Special Regulations” article, as well as amendments to the “Use Regulations.” Recently, two local landowners have met with the Planning Director to inquire about converting existing accessory structures into residential units either for themselves or their family. The Planning Director proposed an amendment to the existing ADU ordinance to allow for ADUs larger than 900 square feet by Special Permit. However, the proposal to reconsider the ADU ordinance was met with pushback. Therefore, the draft amendment below is independent of the ADU ordinance – it is a new zoning ordinance to allow for existing accessory structures, such as barns or carriage houses, built before August 2016 to be converted into single-family homes by Special Permit. The City of Greenfield is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer, a designated Green Community and a recipient of the “Leading by Example” Award Note: Text with a strikethrough is text to be deleted, black bold italic text is newly proposed text. ---ARTICLE VII ~ 200-7.22. Adaptive Residential Reuse of Accessory Structures A. Purpose. The purpose of this Section is to allow the adaptive reuse of existing accessory structures, such as barns, carriage houses, garages, and other structures for residential purposes in any zoning district where residential uses are allowed. This zoning provides for adaptive residential reuse of accessory structures to accomplish the following purposes: (1) Enable homeowners to utilize existing structures on their land for rental income and alternative living options; (2) Support the maintenance of and prevent dilapidation of historical structures; (3) Increase housing options with gentle density that maintains the existing fabric of the built environment; (4) B. Ensure safe and healthy housing compliant with the Building Code. Applicability. (1) See Sections 200-4.1 through 200-4.17 and Appendix A, Table of Uses, for permitting requirements. C. Adaptive Residential Reuse Standards. The Zoning Board of Appeals, acting as the special permit granting authority (SPGA), may grant a special permit to use an existing accessory structure for single-family residential use on a lot with any number of existing dwellings, provided all of the following conditions are satisfied: (1) The accessory structure must have existed continuously since before August 2016 and have a minimum gross floor area of 900 square feet. (2) The accessory structure may be converted to no more than one dwelling unit and must be a complete, separate housekeeping unit containing both kitchen and bath. The City of Greenfield is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer, a designated Green Community and a recipient of the “Leading by Example” Award (3) The accessory structure may not expand in gross floor area or footprint, except for improvements related to fire safety, ADA accessibility, or utilities. (4) The accessory structure may be converted to residential use notwithstanding nonconformity with dimensional requirements, provided that the conversion does not increase the degree of nonconformity. (5) The accessory structure must be and remain located on the same lot. (6) The exterior façade of the accessory structure shall substantially retain its appearance and architectural features shall be preserved to the maximum extent practicable. (7) The construction of any residential unit must be in conformity with the State Building Code, Title V of the State Sanitary Code, 527 CMR – MA Fire Prevention Regulations and other local ordinances and regulations. (8) Prior to issuance of a permit, a floor plan must be submitted showing the proposed interior and exterior changes to the building. (9) For dwellings to be served by on-site septic system, the owner must obtain a letter from the Board of Health stating that the existing sewage disposal system is adequate for the proposed residential use before a Building Permit can be obtained. title: Conservation Commission Public Hearing 6
text: TOWN OF UXBRIDGE CONSERVATION COMMISSION 21 SOUTH MAIN STREET UXBRIDGE, MASSACHUSETTS 01569 508-278-8600 x2020 CONSERVATION PUBLIC HEARING/MEETING NOTICES The Uxbridge Conservation Commission will hold a Public Hearing on Monday December 7, 2026 at 6:30PM in the Board of Selectmen Meeting Room, Town Hall, 21 South Main Street, Uxbridge MA, to review the following application under the MA Wetlands Protection Act (MGL Ch. 131, Sec. 40). Plans may be reviewed in the Conservation office during regular business hours or on the town’s website. Notice of Intent — Filed by Fuss and O'Neil Inc on behalf of Town of Uxbridge Public Works. The proposed Douglas Street (Route 16) Reconstruction project in Uxbridge, Massachusetts. The proposed project involves the reconstruction of approximately 1.9 miles of Douglas Street (Route 16), beginning approximately 300 feet east of the Route 146 northbound ramps and extending easterly to approximately 100 feet west of the intersection with South Main Street (Route 122). An Order of Conditions is required for the proposed work because portions of the project occur within Riverfront Area associated with Cold Spring Brook, a designated Coldwater Fisheries Resource, and Buffer Zone protected under the Massachusetts Wetlands Protection Act (M.G.L. c.131 §40) and its implementing regulations at 310 CMR 10.00. The project area is also located partially within the Town of Uxbridge’s 25- foot No Disturb Zone. The project is anticipated to result in approximately 2,044 square feet of permanent impacts and 11,330 square feet of temporary impacts to the Riverfront Area, as well as 20,219 square feet of permanent impacts and 55,471 square feet of temporary impacts to the Buffer Zone. The proposed work qualifies as a Limited Project under 310 CMR 10.53(3)(f), as it involves minor roadway improvements within an existing developed right-of-way that serves a public transportation purpose. The project has been carefully designed to minimize disturbance to adjacent resource areas and to remain largely within the existing roadway footprint, thereby meeting the intent of the Limited Project provisions for public roadway and access improvements. Submitted by Russ Holden, Chairman, Uxbridge Conservation Commission
